docs.article:
Show your clients who looked#

Studio's Analytics page answers the questions a developer or an agency gets asked after sending a walkthrough link: how many people opened it, how long they stayed, which rooms they spent time in, whether they got as far as asking about the property, and on what devices. Every number can be exported as a CSV or sent as a printable report.

You need: a Studio account and scenes you own (see Share privately for accounts and owned uploads).

1. Open the dashboard#

Sign in at /studio and click Analytics in the top bar, or open a scene's Analytics panel and pick Full analytics & client report.

  • All scenes (the default) adds up every scene you own and lists each one with its views, unique viewers, median time and enquiries. Click a scene to drill into it.
  • 7 / 30 / 90 days picks the range. Days are UTC.
NumberWhat it counts
Viewseach time the link was opened in a browser tab
Unique viewersdifferent browsers (a random id the browser keeps; no name or login)
Returning viewersbrowsers that opened the scene more than once in the range
Median / total timetime the scene was open and on screen (sampled every 2 s; a tab left in the background does not count)
Enquiriesclicks on the scene's enquiry button

2. Add an enquiry button#

The last step of the funnel is your call to action. On a scene's analytics page, under Enquiry button, set a label and a link:

  • https://… — your contact form, a booking page or a WhatsApp link (https://wa.me/91…)
  • mailto:sales@yourcompany.com
  • tel:+91 80 1234 5678

Every viewer of that scene then sees the button over the walkthrough. The funnel reads Opened → Interacted (dragged, tapped, walked or pressed a key) → Stayed 30 s+ → Enquired.

The same setting over the API:

Code
curl -X PUT https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/enquiry -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"label":"Book a site visit","url":"https://wa.me/918012345678"}'

3. Where people looked and which rooms they saw#

For an interior with a floor plan, the scene page shows:

  • Where people looked: a heatmap over the plan. Blue cells show where visitors stood; amber cells show where they waited for the scene to load.
  • Rooms visited: the plan is split into rooms at the doorways (open-plan spaces stay one room, corridors are their own). A room takes the name of a hotspot inside it (author one per room in the default experience, see Author a guided tour), otherwise "Room 1", "Room 2"… from largest to smallest. Rooms nobody entered are listed with 0, which is also worth knowing. Time spent on a terrace or in the garden reads Outdoors; time spent looking at the house from the opening overview reads Overview (outside the floor plan).
  • Name your rooms: click a room on the plan (or ✎ in the list) and type "Kitchen", "Master bedroom"… The name is used everywhere: dashboard, CSV and client report, for past days too.
  • Top viewpoints: the five spots where visitors spent the most time, as "Kitchen · facing north-west", with numbered pins on the plan.

A scene without an interior floor plan (an object, an open-air scene) has no rooms; the dashboard says so and still shows where people looked.

Scenes plan the storey you start on, with interior walls and the garden marked; re-upload an older multi-storey scene (a new version) to get its rooms.

4. Devices#

Phone / tablet / desktop, iOS / Android / desktop systems, the in-app browser (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, LinkedIn…) and how people arrived: a direct link, a private share link or an embed on your site. People opening a share link are counted, but stay anonymous like everyone else.

5. Send it to your client#

  • Download CSV gives the same numbers as a spreadsheet: headline metrics, one row per day, the funnel, rooms and device split (and, for All scenes, one row per scene).
  • Client report opens a clean one-page report for the scene (or all scenes) and range. Press Print / Save as PDF: it prints on white paper, A4, with how it was measured at the bottom.

6. Share a viewer report with a link#

The viewer report is the client-ready page for one scene: who opened it (anonymous viewers, how many times, on what device, and where they came from: WhatsApp, Instagram, Google, an e-mail, your website's embed…), the time spent in each room as a heatmap over the floor plan, the hotspots they opened, how many questions they asked Ask Verse, average and median time, and the funnel to your enquiry button. It works on a phone.

  1. In Studio → Analytics, pick the scene and press Share report (or open Client report and press Share link).
  2. Name the link after who it is for (for example "Sharma family"), pick the window (last 7, 30 or 90 days) and press Create link.
  3. Copy the link and send it. It is shown once — the server keeps only a fingerprint of it.
  4. To stop sharing, press Revoke next to the link. It stops working at once, for the page and the CSV alike. Deleting the scene revokes every link.

Anyone with the link sees the report and can download its CSV. They never see your account, your other scenes or your enquiry link. If the scene is private, the report still opens but does not link to the scene or show the floor-plan image — the rooms are drawn from their outlines instead — so a report link never becomes a way into a private scene. Viewers appear as codes like V-4AF8C3: one code is one browser, never a name.

The same exports over the API: GET /v1/scenes/<id>/analytics.csv?days=30 and GET /v1/account/analytics.csv?days=30; the viewer report is GET /v1/scenes/<id>/report[.csv], its links /v1/scenes/<id>/report/links (API).

Privacy, in short#

  • No names, e-mail addresses, phone numbers or IP addresses are stored for analytics. A visitor is a random id their browser keeps in local storage; the server keeps only a keyed hash of it.
  • Device class, system and in-app browser are worked out **on the device**; the browser's user-agent string is not stored with the analytics rows.
  • Visitors with Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control switched on are never counted. A link with ?analytics=0 is not counted; ?analytics=never turns counting off on that browser for good (?analytics=1 turns it back on); an embed with analytics: false is never counted.
  • Storage is bounded: raw samples live in a rotating log; completed days are kept as daily totals per scene for VERSE_ANALYTICS_KEEP_DAYS (400 days by default) and then deleted. Deleting a scene deletes its analytics.
